title: Dedicated staged rollouts: emit audit log events for rollout actions + export integration
creator: Kaitlyn Nguyen
project: Dedicated staged rollouts for reserved pools
description:
Goal
Add structured audit log events for Dedicated staged rollout actions (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold/rollback/etc) and ensure they flow through the existing audit log export pipeline (SIEM + customer export destinations where enabled).

Context
Dedicated staged rollouts introduces approval-gated state transitions and automated holds/rollbacks based on gate evaluation. Enterprise Dedicated customers have asked for an auditable trail of:
- who made/approved changes
- what changed (plan version, stage weights, gate thresholds)
- when/where it happened (timestamp, region)
- whether a hold/rollback was automatic vs manual

This ticket covers:
1) Event taxonomy + payload fields
2) Emitting events from control plane / console workflows / evaluator
3) Integration with existing audit export pipeline (ensuring events are correctly tagged, routed, retained, and not dropped)

References
- ADR-028: Rollout approvals and audit logging: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-028-rollout-approvals-and-audit-logging.json
- Security spec draft: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/dedicated-rollout-audit-events.json
- Related engineering: ENG-5122 (approval/abort endpoints), ENG-5121 (control-plane schema), ENG-5129 (RBAC)

Event types (v1)
Emit audit events under a stable namespace, e.g. "rollouts.dedicated.*".

Required (beta)
- rollouts.dedicated.plan.created
- rollouts.dedicated.plan.updated
- rollouts.dedicated.plan.deleted (if supported; otherwise omit)
- rollouts.dedicated.approval.requested (when stage requires approval + is ready to advance)
- rollouts.dedicated.approval.granted
- rollouts.dedicated.approval.denied (if we support explicit deny; otherwise omit)
- rollouts.dedicated.rollout.aborted
- rollouts.dedicated.rollout.paused (manual pause action)
- rollouts.dedicated.rollout.resumed (manual resume action)
- rollouts.dedicated.stage.advanced (includes from_stage -> to_stage)
- rollouts.dedicated.stage.rolled_back (manual rollback)
- rollouts.dedicated.gate.failed (gate name/type + measured value + threshold + window)
- rollouts.dedicated.rollout.held (automatic hold due to gate failure OR missing metrics)

Nice-to-have (GA / follow-ups)
- rollouts.dedicated.gate.passed (may be noisy; consider sampling)
- rollouts.dedicated.routing.policy_applied (if we need additional evidence of traffic split enforcement)
- rollouts.dedicated.export.delivered / export.failed (pipeline-level events; likely already present)

Payload fields
All events MUST include (where applicable):
- event_type (string)
- event_id (uuid)
- occurred_at (RFC3339)
- actor_type: user | service | system
- actor_id (internal principal id)
- actor_email (only for internal users; omit for customers if policy requires)
- actor_ip (when available; may be empty for service-to-service)
- user_agent (console actions)
- tenant_id
- org_id (if distinct)
- dedicated_pool_id
- rollout_plan_id
- rollout_plan_version (monotonic integer / etag)
- rollout_id (if distinct from plan; depends on control-plane model)
- stage_id / stage_name
- request_id / trace_id (to correlate)
- region
- outcome: success | failure

Event-specific fields
- plan.created/updated: diff summary fields
  - change_summary (short string; e.g., "Updated stage 2 weight 25%->50%, added gate queue_depth")
  - changed_fields (comma-separated list; low cardinality)
- approval.granted/denied:
  - approval_policy_id (if applicable)
  - approval_comment (optional; truncated)
- gate.failed:
  - gate_type (latency_p95_ms | error_rate_5xx | timeout_rate | gpu_utilization | queue_depth | metrics_freshness)
  - evaluation_window (e.g., "5m")
  - observed_value (string to avoid float parsing issues in downstream; include unit in field name where possible)
  - threshold (string)
  - comparator (>, >=, etc)
- rollout.held:
  - hold_reason (gate_failed | missing_metrics | evaluator_degraded | manual)
  - hold_detail (short)

PII / security constraints
- Do not include prompt text, request payloads, or model outputs.
- Keep actor_email consistent with existing audit policy (internal ok, customer depends on org settings). If unclear, default to actor_id only + actor_type.
- Ensure event payload stays < 16KB; truncate comments/change_summary.
- Ensure tenancy isolation: exports MUST only contain events for that tenant.

Export pipeline integration
- Add new event types to audit log schema registry / allowlist so they are exported (and not dropped as unknown).
- Ensure events are tagged with tenant/org so existing routing works.
- Validate retention: audit logs follow current retention defaults (per Security guidance). Document if rollouts require extended retention for Dedicated contracts.

Implementation notes
- Emit events from the authoritative services:
  - control plane for plan CRUD and state transitions
  - approval endpoints for approval events
  - evaluator for gate_failed + rollout_held (automatic)
- Use idempotency keys to avoid duplicate audit events on retries (especially evaluator tick + approval race).
- Ensure ordering is not strictly required, but include occurred_at + plan_version + stage_id to reconstruct.

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] For each required event type, an event is emitted on the relevant action/state transition in staging and prod.
- [ ] Events show up in the audit log viewer (internal) and are exported via the existing pipeline for allowlisted tenants.
- [ ] Events contain required fields and exclude sensitive content.
- [ ] Duplicate emission rate is negligible; retries do not create unbounded duplicates.
- [ ] Basic integration test: perform create->advance->gate fail->auto hold->manual abort; verify sequence in audit log store.

Testing plan
- Unit tests for event emission per endpoint/state transition.
- Integration test in staging: create rollout plan + progress one stage, then force missing metrics to trigger hold; confirm emitted events.
- Export validation: pick one internal test tenant with SIEM export enabled; verify new event types appear downstream.

Open questions
- Do we include actor_email for enterprise tenant users (future self-serve) or only actor_id? Default to actor_id to align with least-privilege, but confirm with Marcus.
- Is plan.deleted supported in v1? If not, omit and rely on updated+archived state.
- Do we need gate.passed events or just gate.failed + stage.advanced summaries? (Concern: high volume + cardinality.)
